failure_modes: Redundancy mistaken for meta-modularity: identical copies explain survival, not adaptation
Carrying more models than the system can afford to maintain
Failing to notice that the current model has expired, so the alternatives are never used
gloss: Adapt by holding overlapping, non-identical models of the same situation and moving between them cheaply
invariants: The models overlap in domain but differ in content
Inspecting each model reveals the domain it models
Switching between models costs less than rebuilding one from scratch
mechanism: A system keeps a population of overlapping but non-identical models of the same or adjacent domains, as genetic diversity in a population, gene-expression switching in a plant, or E. coli's many metabolic routes do. Because of {{bounded_model_open_world}}, any single model expires. Overlapping models contain information the primary model lacks, so the system can detect expiry and pivot. Contrast multi-modularity (identical spare parts, which solve damage but not novelty) and mono-modularity (one general model applied everywhere, which cannot dominate specialists across all problems).
